import html from string import Template # Predefined template for blog posts. BLOG_FORMAT = """

$title

$body
""" def show_blog_post(headline: str, text: str) -> str: """ Return a sanitized and formatted blog post ready for safe display. Parameters ---------- headline : str The title of the blog post. text : str The main body content of the blog post. Returns ------- str A string containing the HTML snippet for the blog post, with all user supplied content properly escaped. Raises ------ ValueError If the title or body contains characters that would break the template (e.g., unescaped '$' signs). The function escapes all user input, so this exception should not normally occur. """ # Escape user supplied content to avoid XSS and other injection issues. safe_title = html.escape(headline, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(text, quote=True) # Use Template to safely substitute placeholders. try: template = Template(BLOG_FORMAT) formatted_post = template.substitute(title=safe_title, body=safe_body) except KeyError as exc: raise ValueError(f"Missing placeholder in BLOG_FORMAT: {exc}") from exc except ValueError as exc: # Template will raise ValueError if there's an unescaped '$' in user data. raise ValueError("User input contains invalid characters for template substitution.") from exc return formatted_post
